subject: SIG + consolidated third-party inventory for NovaMed evaluation
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@novamed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: consolidated SIG + subprocessor inventory for NovaMed evaluation

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the runtime performance. Procurement asked me to collect a consolidated set of materials so their security review can move forward. Can you share: 

- A current SIG questionnaire (completed or the completed sections you can share) or CAIQ snapshot if easier.
- A consolidated subprocessor inventory (names, purposes, locations, data types processed).
- Any SOC 2 attestation or a recent SOC 2 snapshot we can provide to our security team (or a secure link to download).

We need this to complete our preliminary risk assessment by the end of next week. If there are any items that require an NDA or specific access permissions, let me know and we can route it through procurement.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
Procurement Manager, NovaMed Systems
procurement@novamed.com

P.S. If there's a preferred contact for evidence collection, send that too.

Subject: Re: Request: consolidated SIG + subprocessor inventory for NovaMed evaluation

Hi Sara — great to hear the demo landed well.

We can absolutely provide what you've requested. I've attached a current export of our subprocessor roster (CSV) and a high-level SOC 2 snapshot. For detailed SIG/CAIQ responses we maintain a curated package — we typically share that via a secure link to reduce packaging lag and keep the artifact up to date.

Quick notes:
- The attached subprocessor_inventory_20260520.csv includes processor name, primary purpose, country of processing, and the categories of customer data involved. If you need contact points for any vendor, say which rows and we'll add a vendor owner.
- SOC 2 snapshot is a redacted copy suitable for evaluations; full SOC reports are available under our customer-facing evidence agreement.
- The CAIQ-completed sections live in the Drive link below; if procurement needs an exported PDF we can produce one.

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.redwoodinference.com/s/novamed-evidence-pack-78
Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20260520.csv, soc2_snapshot_2025-12.pdf

If procurement needs a formal NDA before a full SIG export, let me know and we can loop Legal — otherwise we can share an export with non-sensitive fields immediately.

Regards,

Grace — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of internal items before we send the CAIQ: 

1) Deal and evidence labeling: please stamp the Drive export with HubSpot ID HS-00098765 and our internal deal_id NM-2026-EVAL-78 so CS/RevOps can reconcile.
2) Sensitive vendors: there are three vendors in the roster marked as 'security-sensitive' (KMS provider, key telemetry, and captive inference optimizer). We should redact owner contact emails from the public export and instead offer to introduce vendor owners on request.
3) Pricing/procure ask: procurement will likely request a data-subprocessor clause. Can Legal provide our standard subprocessor addendum? Priyom — can you pull the most recent version and confirm whether we have a pre-signed annex for healthcare customers?

If we're OK with the redaction approach we can share the CAIQ sections immediately and follow up with an extended evidence pack behind an access control.

-Rishi
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
